examples.title: Loop language: the basics
examples.summary: Declarations, options, variables, loop, if/elif/else, lists, for, count, log, stop, accept.

examples.title: Loop language: several counterexamples
examples.summary: for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3): several counterexamples per candidate.

examples.title: Loop language: optimal counterexamples
examples.summary: C.solve(assume G(M), optimal): the smallest refinement, with #minimize in the check.

examples.title: Loop language: two checks
examples.summary: Two check solvers with their own fragments and links; the second runs only if the first finds nothing.

examples.title: Loop language: clauses from ASP
examples.summary: reject M with G.clauses(X): the refinement written as clause/3 atoms in ASP.

examples.title: Loop language: unsat cores
examples.summary: reject M with G.core(C): refine from an unsatisfiable core when the check looks for a witness.

examples.title: Loop language: a refinement solver
examples.summary: A third solver R computes the refinement: R.solve(assume GA(M), GC(X)).

examples.title: Loop language: legacy glue
examples.summary: link ... legacy: glue fragments that list the interface atoms themselves (cegar.py files).

examples.title: Loop language: raw Lua
examples.summary: A loop written directly in Lua against the runtime API (rt.solver, rt.link, A:search, ...).

examples.title: Graph colouring, Shape 1
examples.summary: Shape 1: check inside the search. One solve call of A for the whole run; refinements are added as clauses during the search.

examples.title: Graph colouring, Shape 2
examples.summary: Shape 2: solve, check, refine, solve again. A is solved once per candidate.

examples.title: Graph colouring, Shape 3
examples.summary: Shape 3: ground the #program refine(k) part once per counterexample (rules instead of clauses).

examples.title: Graph colouring, Shape 4
examples.summary: Shape 4: search, collect counterexamples, ground the refine part for 20 at a time.

examples.title: Graph colouring, Reference run
examples.summary: Reference run: block each refuted candidate. Always sound; slow, but its count is the truth.

examples.title: Graph colouring
examples.summary: Graphs with a leaf colouring that no 3-colouring extends (n = 6, all 10,698 solutions).

examples.title: Graph colouring (original rules)
examples.summary: The same with the original, too weak relevant/1 rules: 9,270 instead of 10,698.

examples.title: Nash equilibria
examples.summary: Weighted graphs whose colouring game has a Nash equilibrium.

examples.title: Voting: justifications
